questions.question: In which year was the Quit India Movement launched?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress on 8 August 1942 with the call of 'Do or Die'. 1930 marks the Civil Disobedience Movement, while 1945 was the year the Second World War ended.

questions.question: Which river is popularly known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal' because of its devastating floods?
questions.explanation: The Damodar river, a tributary of the Hugli, was notorious for floods in the Bengal region and earned the name 'Sorrow of Bengal'. The Kosi, which floods parts of north Bihar, is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

questions.question: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces?
options: B) The Prime Minister of India
C) The Chief of Defence Staff
D) The Defence Minister of India
questions.explanation: Under Article 53 of the Constitution, the supreme command of the Defence Forces of the Union vests in the President, who exercises it in accordance with law. The Prime Minister heads the government but does not hold this constitutional office.

questions.question: Which Indian state is the largest producer of tea?
questions.explanation: Assam is India's largest tea-producing state, contributing more than half of the country's output. West Bengal (mainly Darjeeling and the Dooars) is the second largest producer.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam, one of the classical dance forms of India, traces its origin to which state?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam developed in the temples of Tamil Nadu, particularly through the Devadasi tradition. Kathakali and Mohiniyattam belong to Kerala, Kuchipudi to Andhra Pradesh and Odissi to Odisha.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President be impeached?
questions.explanation: Article 61 lays down the procedure for impeachment of the President for violation of the Constitution, requiring a charge by either House with a two-thirds majority and investigation by the other House. Article 56 deals with the President's term of office.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 following violence at which place?
questions.explanation: After a mob set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district in February 1922, killing policemen, Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, insisting on non-violence. Champaran is associated with his 1917 indigo satyagraha and Dandi with the 1930 Salt March.

questions.question: Which of the following Dam–River pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
options: B) Sardar Sarovar Dam – Narmada River
C) Nagarjuna Sagar Dam – Krishna River
questions.explanation: The Tehri Dam, India's highest dam, is built on the Bhagirathi river, not the Alaknanda, in Uttarakhand. Sardar Sarovar is on the Narmada, Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna, and Mettur on the Kaveri.

questions.question: Who won the men's singles title at the Wimbledon Championships 2025?
questions.explanation: Italy's Jannik Sinner won his first Wimbledon title in 2025, defeating defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the men's singles final.

questions.question: Who won the Ballon d'Or award for 2024, given to the world's best footballer?
questions.explanation: Spain and Manchester City midfielder Rodri won the 2024 Ballon d'Or, beating Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior, who finished second.

questions.question: Which is India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier?
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant, built by Cochin Shipyard and commissioned in 2022, is India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier. INS Vikramaditya is a refitted import, Viraat was retired, and Arihant is a nuclear submarine.

questions.question: The 2026 Asian Games are scheduled to be hosted by which city/region of Japan?
questions.explanation: The 20th Asian Games in 2026 are scheduled to be hosted by the Aichi-Nagoya region of Japan. Tokyo hosted the 1964 Olympics, while the 2025 World Expo was held in Osaka.

questions.question: Which country won the gold medal in the Open section of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in 2024?
questions.explanation: India won gold in both the Open and the Women's sections of the 45th Chess Olympiad held at Budapest, Hungary, in September 2024, topping the Open section for the first time in its Olympiad history.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka in September 2024?
questions.explanation: Harini Amarasuriya, a National People's Power Member of Parliament, was sworn in as Prime Minister of Sri Lanka on 24 September 2024 in the government of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, becoming the third woman to hold the post.

questions.question: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries concerning which of the following?
options: A) Discovery of the yellow fever virus and its vaccine
B) Peripheral immune tolerance mediated by regulatory T cells
C) Development of the mRNA vaccine platform
D) MicroRNAs and their role in gene regulation
questions.explanation: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi for their discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance, centred on regulatory T cells, which prevent the immune system from attacking the body's own tissues.

questions.question: Find the next term of the series: 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, ?
questions.explanation: Each term from the third onward is the sum of the two preceding terms: 1+3=4, 3+4=7, 4+7=11, 7+11=18. Hence the next term is 11+18 = 29.

questions.question: Complete the letter series: Z, W, T, Q, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back in the alphabet: Z to W, W to T, T to Q, and Q to N. Hence the next letter is N.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'sky is blue' is written as 'pa da na', 'blue is deep' is written as 'na ka pa', and 'sea is deep' is written as 'ka ra na'. What is the code for the word 'blue'?
questions.explanation: Comparing the first and third sentences, the only common word 'is' has the common code 'na'. Comparing the second and third sentences, 'deep' is the common word with common code 'ka'. In 'blue is deep' = 'na ka pa', the remaining code 'pa' must stand for 'blue'.

questions.question: Select the pair that completes the analogy: Stethoscope : Doctor :: Compass : ?
questions.explanation: A stethoscope is the characteristic working tool of a doctor; similarly, a compass is the characteristic working tool of a navigator, used to find direction.

questions.question: Select the pair that best completes the analogy: Bird : Nest :: Bee : ?
questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest, just as a bee lives in a hive. The relationship is 'animal : dwelling place'.

questions.question: A is the brother of B. C is the mother of A. D is the father of C. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of A, and D is the father of C. So D is the father of A's mother, i.e. D is A's (maternal) grandfather.

questions.question: A woman walks 5 km towards the east, then turns to her left and walks 12 km. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: The eastward 5 km and the southward 12 km (a left turn from east) are perpendicular, so the distance from the start is sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(169) = 13 km.

questions.question:
Find the missing number in the grid:
Row 1: 2, 5, 8
Row 2: 4, ?, 16
Row 3: 6, 15, 24
questions.explanation: In each row, the middle number is the average of the two end numbers: (2+8)/2 = 5 and (6+24)/2 = 15. Applying the same rule to Row 2: (4+16)/2 = 10.

questions.question: In a school of 800 students, 55% are girls. How many boys are there in the school?
questions.explanation: Girls = 55% of 800 = 440. Boys = 800 − 440 = 360. Alternatively, boys form 45% of 800 = 360.

questions.question: The average of five numbers 7, 11, 15, 19 and x is 14. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Total of the five numbers = 5 × 14 = 70. Sum of the four known numbers = 7 + 11 + 15 + 19 = 52. Hence x = 70 − 52 = 18.

questions.question: If x + y = 12 and xy = 27, what is the value of x^2 + y^2?
The average weight of 6 members of a group is 52 kg. If one member weighing 60 kg leaves the group, what is the average weight of the remaining members?
questions.explanation: Total weight = 6 × 52 = 312 kg. After the 60 kg member leaves, total = 312 − 60 = 252 kg over 5 members, giving an average of 252 ÷ 5 = 50.4 kg.

questions.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures 150 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle = 180 − 150 = 30 degrees, and the exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360 degrees. Number of sides = 360 ÷ 30 = 12.

questions.question: What is the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × pi × r^3 = (4/3) × pi × 27 = 36pi cm^3, which is about 113.1 cm^3.

questions.question:
The table below shows the number of four types of trees planted in a colony over a year.
Tree type   | Mango | Neem | Peepal | Banyan
Number      |  120  |  90  |   60   |   30
What percentage of the total trees planted were Mango trees?
questions.explanation: Total trees = 120 + 90 + 60 + 30 = 300. Mango trees form 120/300 × 100 = 40% of the total.

questions.question: The price of a gadget first increases by 20% and then decreases by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the price?
questions.explanation: Take the original price as 100. After a 20% increase it becomes 120; a 20% decrease on 120 gives 120 − 24 = 96. The net change is 100 → 96, i.e. a 4% decrease.

questions.question: If x − y = 4 and xy = 45, what is the value of x + y?
questions.explanation: (x + y)^2 = (x − y)^2 + 4xy = 4^2 + 4 × 45 = 16 + 180 = 196. Since x + y is positive here (as xy > 0 with x − y > 0), x + y = 14.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions. Decide which conclusion follows.
Statements: All pens are pencils. All pencils are erasers.
Conclusion I: All pens are erasers.
Conclusion II: Some erasers are pencils.
options: B) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
D) Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Since all pens are pencils and all pencils are erasers, all pens are erasers — I follows. 'All pencils are erasers' converts to 'Some erasers are pencils', so II also follows. Hence both conclusions follow.

questions.question: If 1 January 2026 falls on a Thursday, what day of the week will 15 August 2026 be?
questions.explanation: 2026 is not a leap year. 15 August is day 227 of the year (31+28+31+30+31+30+31+15 = 227). Since 1 January 2026 is a Thursday, day number n falls on weekday ((n−1) mod 7) days after Thursday. 227 − 1 = 226, and 226 mod 7 = 2, so 15 August is 2 weekdays after Thursday, i.e. Saturday.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 5 o'clock?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark subtends 30 degrees (360/12). At 5 o'clock the hands are 5 hour-marks apart, so the angle is 5 × 30 = 150 degrees.

questions.question: Five friends G, H, I, J and K are sitting in a row facing the same direction. I sits exactly in the middle. G sits at the extreme left. H sits immediately to the left of I. J sits immediately to the right of I. Who sits at the extreme right?
questions.explanation: Positions 1 to 5: G is fixed at position 1 and I at position 3 (middle). H immediately left of I takes position 2, and J immediately right of I takes position 4. The only person left, K, must sit at position 5 — the extreme right.

questions.question: Four workshops — Painting, Music, Dance and Yoga — are held on four consecutive days from Monday to Thursday, one per day. Music is held on Wednesday. Painting is held on the day immediately before Music. Yoga is not held on Monday. On which day is the Dance workshop held?
questions.explanation: Painting is immediately before Music (Wednesday), so Painting is on Tuesday. Yoga is not on Monday, so Yoga is on Thursday. That leaves Dance for Monday.

questions.question: In a class of 40 students, Rahul ranks 11th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Rank from bottom = (Total − Rank from top) + 1 = 40 − 11 + 1 = 30. So Rahul ranks 30th from the bottom.

questions.question:
Amit, Bina, Carlos and Dev each live in a different one of four cities: Delhi, Jaipur, Kochi and Pune, and each owns a different pet: cat, dog, parrot and rabbit.
(i) Amit lives in Delhi.
(ii) Bina lives in Kochi and owns the parrot.
(iii) Carlos owns the dog.
(iv) Dev lives in Pune and does not own the rabbit.
Where does Carlos live, and who owns the rabbit?
options: A) Carlos lives in Jaipur, and Dev owns the rabbit
B) Carlos lives in Jaipur, and Carlos owns the rabbit
C) Carlos lives in Jaipur, and Amit owns the rabbit
D) Carlos lives in Pune, and Amit owns the rabbit
questions.explanation: Amit is in Delhi, Bina in Kochi and Dev in Pune, so Carlos must live in the only remaining city, Jaipur. Bina owns the parrot and Carlos the dog, leaving the cat and the rabbit for Amit and Dev. Since Dev does not own the rabbit, Dev owns the cat and Amit owns the rabbit.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is essential for the formation of rhodopsin, the visual pigment of the retina. Its deficiency causes night blindness. Vitamin B1 deficiency causes beriberi, Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy and Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets.

questions.question: Which green pigment in leaves absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy and drives photosynthesis. Haemoglobin is a blood pigment, carotene an accessory orange pigment, and melanin the skin pigment.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure wind speed?
questions.explanation: An anemometer measures wind speed. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, a hygrometer measures humidity, and a seismograph records earthquake waves.

questions.question: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer located?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer lies in the lower stratosphere, roughly 15–35 km above the Earth's surface, where ozone absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.question: Dengue is transmitted to humans by the bite of which mosquito?
questions.explanation: Dengue is spread by the female Aedes aegypti mosquito, which bites during the daytime. Anopheles transmits malaria, while Culex and Mansonia spread filariasis and Japanese encephalitis.

questions.question: Which acid is present in curd (dahi)?
questions.explanation: Curd is formed when bacteria ferment lactose (milk sugar) into lactic acid, which gives curd its sour taste. Citric acid is in citrus fruits, acetic acid in vinegar and tartaric acid in tamarind.

questions.question: The 'Yellow Revolution' in India is associated with the increased production of which crop group?
questions.explanation: The Yellow Revolution is associated with the rise in oilseed production (mustard, sunflower, groundnut and others), driven by the Technology Mission on Oilseeds launched in 1986. The Blue Revolution relates to fish production, the White Revolution to milk, and the Silver Revolution to egg production.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on Rs 6,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?

A man borrows Rs 5,000 at 10% per annum. He repays Rs 2,000 at the end of the first year and clears the rest at the end of the second year with compound interest (compounded annually). How much does he pay at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: After one year the debt grows to 5000 × 1.10 = Rs 5,500. He repays Rs 2,000, leaving Rs 3,500 outstanding. In the second year this earns 10% interest: 3500 × 1.10 = Rs 3,850, which he pays at the end of the second year.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone can do it in 12 days. If B works alone, how many days will he take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: B's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24. So B alone completes the work in 24 days.

questions.question: A 180 m long train running at 54 km/h crosses a platform in 20 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation: Speed = 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. In 20 seconds the train covers 15 × 20 = 300 m, which equals its own length plus the platform length. Platform = 300 − 180 = 120 m.
